A.claim: Beal is equivalent to: 2 is an obligatory exponent for every non-trivial primitive solution in the hyperbolic regime. Of the ten coprime Fermat-Catalan solutions listed in the external survey, the nine whose identities verify all have 2 among their exponents.

B.claim: The ordering of Z enters a proof of Beal at exactly one point: positivity forbids cancellation, giving A^x < C^z, B^y < C^z and C^z <= 2 max(A^x,B^y). Hence with A^x <= B^y, C is pinned to within a factor 2^(1/z) <= 1.26 of B^(y/z). Over Z[i] this fails completely - the Helenius identity collapses norm 125 summands to a norm 16 sum.
